THE UNITED REPUBLIC OF TANZANIA STATEMENT BY H.E. DEOGRATIUS JOHN NDEJEMBI, VICE PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED REPUBLIC OF TANZANIA, AT THE GENERAL DEBATE OF THE 81ST SESSION OF THE UNITED NATIONS GENERAL ASSEMBLY NEW YORK 22ND SEPTEMBER 2026
preamble
• H.E. Dr. Khalilur Rahman, President of the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly;
• H.E. António Guterres, Secretary-General of the United Nations;
• Excellencies, Heads of State and Government;
• Distinguished Delegates;

1. Courtesy It is indeed a great honor and privilege to address this Assembly on behalf of H.E. Dr. Samia Suluhu Hassan, President of the United Republic of Tanzania.
H.E. the President asked me to convey her fraternal greetings and best wishes for the success of this Session.
Allow me to congratulate you, on your election to preside over the 81st Session of the UN General Assembly.
Your immense experience and diplomatic skills give us confidence in your ability to guide the proceedings of this Session successfully.
Your election is also a fitting tribute to your great country, Bangladesh, with which Tanzania enjoys excellent relations.

2. Theme of UNGA81 and UN80 Initiatives About eighty years ago, the UN was founded in San Francisco on a simple but enduring principle: that nations can prevent war and advance peace through trust, collective action and respect for the UN Charter.

4. Climate Action face unjustifiable obstacles, mainly Our efforts to address climate-related challenges continue from those to contributing significantly to greenhouse gas emissions.

Global efforts to address climate challenges are being frustrated by withdrawal of financial contributions supporting climate adaptation measures and initiatives by international and regional institutions, as well as individual states.
Let us prioritize delivery on the pledges for climate action by increasing long-term concessional financing and deployment of new technology.
On this agenda, Tanzania chose to address the just energy transition component through different measures.

Some of these measures include, implementation of the national renewable energy strategy that comprises 2,115MW Julius Nyerere Hydro Power Project, 650MW solar and wind power projects, 130MW geothermal power projects, and the National Clean Cooking Strategy, which aims to ensure that 80% of households adopt clean cooking by 2034.
In our efforts to reduce the use of fossil fuels, we have also opted for the electric railway to link the port of Dar es Salaam and neighboring countries of Burundi and DRC.
SIT_COD
We, therefore, appeal that climate financing be provided as grants and concessional financing to step up efforts on climate action.
Tanzania joins Small Islands and Coastal States in pushing for a workable solution to address sea-level rise.

We commend the President for convening today the High-Level Event addressing the existential threats posed by sea-level rise, and we look forward to the adoption of the UN Declaration on Sea-Level Rise, which will provide a comprehensive framework for international cooperation, scientific advancement, adaptation resilience, and legal stability.

We welcome the Declaration's legal affirmation on the stability of maritime zones under United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) and the continuity of statehood, even in cases of physical land loss, while encouraging strengthened international cooperation and the protection of human rights.
HUM1
Timely and urgent action is needed to safeguard the future of our coastal communities and island nations.
5. Sanctions and Embargoes Global solidarity must be concurrent with respect of each other's sovereignty.

Tanzania stands against the proliferating trend of some states to assume the responsibility of policing and imposing unilateral sanctions on others, thus undermining the principles of sovereignty and peaceful co-existence.

As stated previously, Tanzania reaffirms its position to oppose the use of such coercive measures against any Member State and reaffirms its unwavering solidarity with Cuba, Zimbabwe and all other states that are subjected to such unjustifiable constraints.

In line with our resolve to leave no one behind, we call for an immediate and unequivocal lifting of these measures that cause hardships, constrain development and obstruct full enjoyment of human rights.
6. Global Peace and Security Global peace and security are vital for sustainable socio-economic development.
The United Nations, through its Charter, has remained central to international efforts to maintain peace and security, uphold international law, and promote conditions conducive to development.
However, despite these longstanding commitments, the persistence of armed conflicts around the world reflects the departure from the purposes and principles of the Charter.
In addition, there are emerging challenges to the authority of the United Nations Charter and the established often without principles commensurate accountability.

These developments underscore the urgent need to reaffirm multilateralism, strengthen respect for international law, and reinforce the central role of the United Nations in maintaining international peace and security.

8. Tribute to the outgoing UN Secretary-General On behalf of the people of the United Republic of Tanzania, I wish to pay tribute to H.E. António Guterres as he concludes his distinguished tenure as the Secretary-General of the UN.

During his tenure, he steered the UN through an exceptionally challenging period marked by conflicts, geopolitical tensions, the COVID-19 pandemic, climate emergencies and growing pressure on multilateralism.
In all these situations, he remained firm and undeterred.

Tanzania appreciates his support for Africa’s aspirations for peace, sustainable development, climate justice and a fairer international financial architecture, as well as his personal engagement with our country.

Similar accolades are for Ambassador Amina Mohammed, Deputy Secretary-General, who has played a pivotal role in advancing the SDGs, advocacy for women, children and those whose voices are too often unheard.
We shall miss your contribution, but Africa is proud to welcome its daughter back home.
To both of you, we wish you every success and fulfillment in the years ahead.
9. Conclusion In conclusion, I wish to underscore that the UN must not merely reflect on the balance of power but serve as a platform for justice, solidarity, and progress.

As we take stock of its invaluable contribution to the advancement of international peace and humanity, maintenance of security, sustainable development over the past 81 years, let us be reminded that there are more mountains to climb and milestones to accomplish.
Tanzania believes that it is only by respecting and living by the Charter that we can honor the past and build a safer and better future for all.
